evidence.note: Title states a specific, declarative finding in one sentence with no trailing full stop or hook: 'A shared rooftop array could undercut what blocks C and D pay for daytime power'.

Title is a precise finding ('About 40% of what flats ... spend on electricity falls in daylight hours'), but the on-slide evidence is the £612 median stat; the 40% figure only appears in the reader note, a slight title/evidence mismatch.
Resident quote is presented verbatim under a neutral label ('Resident, block D') with a survey cite; no editorialising inside the tile.
Finding title plus short concrete bullets ('64 kW, £86,400 installed', 'Five-year service plan'); plain, no filler.
Body line 'Heavy daytime users get the largest credit.' and notes explain mechanism plainly cause to consequence (array feeds landlord supply, credit split pro rata).
Title lists the three risks as a declarative claim; notes flag 'Single-sourced' and 'Disputed' payback plainly with both figures; no aphorisms or antitheses anywhere in the deck.
Byline reads 'Energy working group, November 2026' rather than the profile's '<presenter name>, <Month year>' form; minor lapse.
Closing title 'The board is asked to approve the £86,400 pilot, with a go or stop review at twelve months' is a plain statement of the ask, slightly procedural rather than a finding.

rationale: Titles are complete, specific single-sentence claims without hooks, wordplay or trailing stops, and body copy, notes and the verbatim quote follow the profile's plain cause-to-consequence, no-aphorism rules throughout. The few lapses are minor: a byline that departs from the profile's name format, a s-2 title whose figure sits only in the note, and a procedural rather than finding-style close. That fits level 4.
